Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Titan Company Limited's Q2 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there 
will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need 
assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on 
your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Ajoy Chawla, Managing Director, Titan Company 
Limited. Thank you, and over to you, Mr. Chawla. 
Ajoy Chawla: 
Thank you. Good evening to everybody on the call. Thank you for being part of this. It has been 
another very fulfilling quarter. We have seen fantastic growth at a consolidated level across most 
of our brands and businesses, and all of them clocking in very healthy growths, driven, of course, 
by a lot of focus on innovation and prioritizing growth over everything else, given the 
opportunity that India offers. It looks like very exciting times for us, despite it being a very 
volatile quarter in terms of some macros. But overall, a very, very good quarter. 
 
With that, I hand over to Ashok, our CFO, to share some opening remarks. 
Ashok Sonthalia: 
Thank you, Ajoy. Good evening, everyone. I just thought I will take this opportunity to clarify 
on particularly two items, so that we all are on same page. One is related to customs duty gains. 
We continue to, as we spoke after quarter one, this quarter also saw a good amount of customs 
duty gain, which is estimated at ₹490 crores for quarter two in Titan Jewellery division and ₹46 
crores in CaratLane. Normalized margin, once you do adjustment for this, on Titan Jewellery 
business would be 11.1%.  
The other thing in jewellery, which we have spoken last time, that a large part of MTM gain of 
quarter one reversed this quarter, which would impact jewellery margin by about 60 basis points. 
And if you normalize for that, then TMZ, which is Titan Jewellery business margin, would be 
11.7%. 
 
Another important item, which is rather new on our P&L, on the face of P&L we have disclosed 
it separately, is related to liability towards the second tranche for the Damas acquisition. This 
amount is ₹671 crores. As per Ind AS 109, any financial liability has to be fair valued at every 
accounting period. 
 
And with the current environment, when we looked at our liability at the end of four years, which 
was accounted for in our books of accounts at ₹1,668 crores, the reassessed liability is less by 
₹671 crores. Please note that this assessment will happen at the end of every quarter, and 
depending on the recovery trajectory of the Damas, there could be pluses and minuses on account 
of this. 
 
But we will continue to disclose it separately so that everyone can understand the nature of that 
number, and all other performance metrics are looked at normalizing for this adjustment. We 

 
 
Titan Company Limited
 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 17 
Sensitivity: Internal
continue to certainly believe in the long-term opportunity that Damas represents, and we believe 
as soon as the geopolitical environment and the conflict situation improves, all the investments 
are in place to ensure that that long-term opportunity gets realized at the Titan group level. 
 
With that, I will open the floor for questions, and we will be very happy to answer. All of us are 
here to answer your questions. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much, Sir. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. The first 
question is from the line of Videesha Sheth from Ambit Capital. Please go ahead. 
Videesha Sheth: 
Hi. My first question was on domestic jewellery EBIT margin. In case of Tanishq, Mia and 
Zoya, you have talked about investments going to higher competition. So which price points or 
categories or regions is this persisting in? When you talk about investments, are there any 
incremental schemes beyond the 0% deduction on old gold, or is it more from an ad campaign 
perspective? 
 
Just in continuation to this, even CaratLane has seen pressure on margins from 10.2% in the base 
period to 6.5%. Does the same competition argument apply there from the challenger daily wear 
brand, or has it got to do with the festive shift? That would be my first question. 
Ashok Sonthalia: 
So, let me take this question and then maybe Arun and Saumen can add to that. I am Ashok here. 
Since increase in customs duty, the domestic market has been operating at a discount compared 
to international. I am talking about gold prices. That leads to the gold price realization pressure. 
We also must understand that this is the second, the other side of the coin. One side is the customs 
duty gain of ₹490 crores, and this pressure is the other side of the coin. So we are normalizing 
that gain completely, and we are talking this in isolation. Actually, we should look at both sides 
of the coin, that we are gaining on customs duty, but there is certainly pressure on gold price 
realization because the entire market is doing that. 
 
As far as CaratLane is concerned, they have making a conscious choice to invest on brand 
building and some of the talent-related investments. And of course, the promotional offers, 
etcetera, were at elevated level in this quarter. 
 
But if you look at the entire H1 margin profile of CaratLane, still remains healthy, still remains 
as per our plan that gradually their EBIT margin should start inching up from 8%  to 9%, and 
then further from there in next couple of years. But anything, Arun, Saumen, you want to add? 
Saumen Bhaumik: 
No, I am done. 
Ashok Sonthalia: 
Yes. Yes. No, so that is what, if I do not know whether… 
Videesha Sheth: 
Got it. No, that answers. And the second one is if you can share your observations on the 
secondary and consumer level trends during this festive versus last festive across all your 
consumer segments? 

 
 
Titan Company Limited
 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 17 
Sensitivity: Internal
Arun Narayan: 
Okay, Arun here. I will start with Tanishq, Mia, Zoya. This year festive pretty much can be seen 
in three phases. The first phase of Navratri from October 11 to October 22, then the second phase 
in between, and now we are in the last leg with Dhanteras tomorrow.  
The first phase of Navratri, we saw good consumers, positive consumer sentiments and good 
traffic to our stores. Pretty much from the day of Vijayadashami for the next few days, there was 
some softness owing to gold rate volatility, which kept customers away. But pretty much from 
the last weekend, which was October 31, we have seen customers come back as we saw an all-
time low perhaps of the last many months, last weekend. 
 
At an overall level from the start of the festive season till today, gold is kind of softer, which is 
bringing back customers in, and we hope to see a pretty strong ending to the season over the 
next few days till November 10. So a very strong start, a very expected strong ending, but a few 
days in between that were a little soft.  
On the qualitative side, I think it has been a good run on studded jewellery sustains. As you 
recall, this began for us pretty much the start of this calendar year. So we have seen three quarters 
of good studded growth, which continues during the festive as well. 
 
And overall, so far, there has been a greater demand for adornment and greater demand for core 
jewellery, while there is the softness on coins and investment buying, which began in quarter 
two, which we saw towards August and September. We see that sustaining during festive as 
well. Although we see the peak of investment buying in the last few days. So we could see 
perhaps some greater interest today, tomorrow, and through the weekend. But so far, it seems 
like a soft interest in investment buying and a greater interest in buying studded and gold 
jewellery. 
Saumen Bhaumik: 
And just to add from CaratLane, during the 24 days of festive season, we, barring for one week, 
I think we have seen a very healthy growth in terms of both revenue as well as buyer growth. 
So, tomorrow is really the day, and hopefully things work out. 
Videesha Sheth: 
Thanks. Watches and eyewear, if there are any quick thoughts? 
Ashok Sonthalia: 
Yes, just watches, but if there is anything. 
Kuruvilla Markose: 
Festive was. This is Diny here. Watches, generally festive doesn't really do that well, but this 
time around, in October, we had pretty good growth, better than Q2. The momentum looks good, 
and particularly in the price points of ₹25,000 to ₹1 lakh, which is an area that we have been 
gaining share, we have done really well. 
Videesha Sheth: 
Thanks for that. I will get back in the queue. 
Ajoy Chawla: 
Eyewear is not driven by festive. 
Videesha Sheth: 
Yes. 

 
 
Titan Company Limited
 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 17 
Sensitivity: Internal
Ajoy Chawla: 
Eyewear does not have a festive SKU, so it may not be relevant. 
Videesha Sheth: 
Yes, sure. Thanks for that. I will get back in the queue. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Devanshu Bansal from Emkay Global. Please go 
ahead. 
Devanshu Bansal: 
Hi, Sir. Thanks for taking my question. Gold price has been on a dipping trend. The benefit in 
H2 will reduce further from gold price perspective. Wanted to check, in the interim, we did take 
some initiatives around light weighting, lower cartages, etcetera, when gold price was going up. 
Wanted to check if we can do some assortment correction to sort of build volumes when the 
gold price is sort of on a dipping trend. If you could share some views on that? 
Arun Narayan: 
Yes, I think it is a relevant question given that situation. And we have been working on 18-carat 
gold for core gold jewellery, both in wedding and daily wears, and also 14-carat in Tanishq 
studded jewellery and up to nine-carat in Mia. And so far, it has built a good catalogue and a 
good availability across stores in the last 9 to 10 months, and it is growing at a very fast clip, 
and we are seeing good adoption by customers, both in traditional gold, 18-carat, as well as 
studded jewellery in 14-carat. 
 
Obviously, there is a geographic skew to that, and some geographies are adopting much faster, 
like the North and the West. But overall, very happy with the way the customer response has 
been to lower cartages.  
Light weighting, I think, has been there for the last two to three years. In fact, ever since COVID, 
we have been kind of focusing on making jewellery more accessible, and that has been an 
ongoing trend. And we are also adding things like detachables and multiple ways of wearing 
jewellery through modularity. So, many things that are ongoing, but the results are quite 
satisfactory. 
Devanshu Bansal: 
Sure. Sir, my question was, can we think of reversing these initiatives? Because now the gold 
price benefit will be relatively lower, and maybe we need to sort of increase volume. Is there 
any thought process around going back to 22-carat sort of jewellery? 
Arun Narayan: 
No, I think as a market leader, the objective is to give choices to customers and leave it to 
customers as to what to buy. We have a very good assortment of 22-carat. Whatever we have 
done is without really compromising the core of Tanishq, and it is really an add-on choice. And 
I think that is the fundamental role of a retailer, to give choice to customers and then allow 
customers to choose what is in their interest. 
 
I do not think we are trying to navigate the ship based on short-term movements. I think in the 
long run, it will help us be accessible, it will help us gain customer share, help us gain buyer 
growth. So, it is a strategic tool which we think will give us a greater customer preference, and 
therefore not something to kind of chop and change based on movements in gold rate. It is a 
long-term strategic decision we have taken, and we would like to stick with it. 

 
 
Titan Company Limited
 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 6 of 17 
Sensitivity: Internal
Devanshu Bansal: 
Got it. Sir, just last one book-keeping. The board has approved raising of ₹2,500 crores capital. 
Wanted to check, is this restructuring or fresh capital that we are raising in the business? 
Ashok Sonthalia: 
This is a replenishment of some of the existing borrowing. It is not additional borrowing. 
Devanshu Bansal: 
Got it, Sir. Thanks for taking my questions. Festive greetings. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Mihir Shah from Nomura. Please go ahead. 
Mihir Shah: 
I’m checking if I'm audible. 
Ajoy Chawla: 
Yes, you are audible. 
Mihir Shah: 
Good evening. Thank you for taking my question. Apologies if this is a repetitive question 
because I joined a bit late. Just wanted to check on the jewellery margin bit. I mean, there was 
an MTM impact that we had seen which was going to happen, which would have actually 
impacted this quarter margin. So, the 11.1% that we are seeing, is there any impact of MTM 
sitting out there? If one has to strip that out, what is the level of margin that one can see? 
Ashok Sonthalia: 
We answered actually upfront, and we were saying that normalized for MTM is 11.7%. The 
other point, since you asked it, I want to add, with the current, the way gold price behaves, the 
way our volume and forwards, futures, etcetera, valuation happens, it has become part and parcel 
of our P&L that 40-50 basis point of MTM pluses, minuses will keep happening, and we need 
to live with this. 
 
This is the thought I am leaving that we should not all the time be very worried about some of 
these things. These 40, 50, 60 basis point MTM pluses, minuses will keep happening quarter on 
quarter. 
Mihir Shah: 
No, absolutely appreciate that, Ashok sir. I just wanted to understand because if your gold coin 
sales, which had become closer to mid-teens, which is like a 2%, 3% margin business, if I am 
not mistaken, has reduced in high single digits, that actually gives a kicker to the margin profile. 
That one was hoping to see a better margin profile than 11.1% is why I asked that question. 
 
In continuation with that, given I think I heard Arun mentioning that investment-led jewellery 
demand is lower. Should one expect in the near term, at least because of this mix shift or mix 
change that we are undergoing in the near term, can one expect margin profiles to be tad higher 
than the 11% mark that we have been doing? 
Ashok Sonthalia: 
I think we still, Mihir, would like to anchor our margin target at around 11%. Growth remains a 
priority. As I spoke about in also, that the way gold prices are behaving in Indian market, because 
of various reasons, they are many times at discount to international prices. There are different 
kind of pulls and pressure in the market, and which we also need to respond to. We would not, 
as far as FY27 is concerned, change our stance on margins. 

 
 
Titan Company Limited
 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 7 of 17 
Sensitivity: Internal
Mihir Shah: 
Understood. Fair point. Secondly, on October sales, specifically not on the festive demand. I 
heard your reply on festive demand. But only on October sales, given that there will be a case 
of lapping of 40% plus base from going forward, how should one think about the buyer growth, 
footfalls, or the October demand? Any colour on that front actually will be very helpful. 
Arun Narayan: 
No, nothing that you should read for the month of October because it's not a like-to-like kind of 
base. We'll perhaps update post at the next interaction to give you a longer-term sense of things. 
Because of the shift, it's a significant shift. So, yes. 
Mihir Shah: 
Any near-term colour, Arun, if you can share on how one should think about Q3, Q4 revenue 
growth momentum because of the base and the way gold prices are going down? 
Arun Narayan: 
No, I think really what is a priority for us, which we had mentioned also in the analyst meet, our 
number one priority is to drive buyer growth, and everything we are doing is to drive buyer 
growth. The cushion that we may get on gold rate-related ticket size is a little, let's say, external 
to whatever we do. 
 
Therefore, everything that we do is to do with driving buyer growth. In quarters ahead, if we 
project that we may not get too much of cushion on the gold rate, we would step up our efforts 
to drive buyer growth. And particularly in the core jewellery, without really worrying or focusing 
on coins and investment-related purchases. So that's where our focus will always be. In times 
when we don't get that cushion, we will work doubly hard to drive buyer growth. Like the first 
quarter was almost a doubling. Last quarter was a 47% jump in gold rate versus last year. This 
quarter may be in a single digit, the way things are going. So that puts a greater responsibility 
on us to drive buyer growth, keeping in mind the CAGR and the goal that we have set for 
ourselves, which is a longer-term plan that we have shared with you all. 
Mihir Shah: 
Understood. Fair point. No, I appreciate that point. Lastly, if I can just quickly check on watch 
margins. I believe they were quite good. Any colour you can share on the reasons for the drivers 
for the watch margin and how should one think about I mean, of course, maybe these may not 
be sustainable ones, but maybe is there a case for a near-term sustainability of sorts on near-term 
watch margins? 
Kuruvilla Markose: 
Diny here. This quarter, we've had a really good story on Edge, driven partly by the Made in 
India: A Titan Story piece, as well as the launch of a good set of products that took price points 
up and therefore margins up. So that was beneficial. But even across the other categories, like I 
mentioned, the ₹25,000 and above price point sales was also really positive. So that is largely 
the reason for the better margin performance, and we certainly hope it will continue. 
Mihir Shah: 
Got it. Thank you very much, and wishing all the very best. 
Kuruvilla Markose: 
Thank you. 
Arun Narayan: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Jay Doshi from Kotak Securities. Please go ahead. 

 
 
Titan Company Limited
 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 8 of 17 
Sensitivity: Internal
Jay Doshi: 
Hi. Thanks for the opportunity. Two questions from my side. First one is the clear improvement 
in studded growth that you are seeing during the course of this calendar year. Is that an industry-
wide sort of phenomenon, or are you benefiting from Diamond Expertise Centres that you are 
setting up? Can you give us some colour on that? 
Arun Narayan: 
No, I think to be honest about this, it is an industry-wide phenomenon. As you are aware, we are 
a low diamond penetration country. And perhaps over the last couple of years, the move was 
towards buying gold jewellery given the pace at which gold was appreciating. And from January 
of this year, we are seeing a secular trend where customers are demonstrating greater interest in 
natural diamonds. 
 
It is a month-on-month sustainable kind of track. But we think it is an industry-wide thing. As 
far as the benefits of Diamond Expertise Centre, it will play out over time. We have now reached 
about 250+ stores. So it is a longer-term move, and it will perhaps play out or give benefit in the 
coming months. 
Ajoy Chawla: 
I will add a flavour to it. Ajoy here. I also believe as a country, we are young. A lot of young 
customers are entering the market. So we are seeing that reflect across the entire portfolio. And 
younger segments are quite comfortable buying studded jewellery. 
 
That is the reading I would pick up. It may be a thin slice, but at least three, four brands that I 
see, there is a certain positive upswing. Therefore, CaratLane is doing well, Mia is doing well, 
and several other players are also picking up good volume. That could be another force at play. 
Jay Doshi: 
Understood. Now on plain gold jewellery growth this quarter, it was a tad softer than what 
perhaps we were hoping for. Have you seen any slowdown or higher competitive intensity, any 
particular region that is dragging down the growth for you? Or was this 20% odd growth, 
basically, I mean, slower growth in plain gold jewellery similar across all the regions? 
Arun Narayan: 
No, I think it's an industry-wide phenomenon. Many players have experienced similar softness 
in the last month of last quarter, and we saw that play out last year as well as customers wait for 
better gold rates, given their understanding of how things may change closer to festive. It's not 
to do with competitive pressure, but I think everyone has seen that softness in September. 
 
And if you knock off the coins part purely in core jewellery sense, perhaps it's a few percentage 
points better. Once you add coins to it looks the way it looks. And even if you see the WGC, 
World Gold Council data for quarter two, you will see that there has been a significant drop as 
an industry on coins and bars. So you need to separate that out, and perhaps it looks a little better. 
But notwithstanding that, there has been, let's say, a pent-up demand as we enter the festive 
season, perhaps in gold jewellery. 
Jay Doshi: 
Sure. One last one, if I may. 
Ajoy Chawla: 
Please go ahead. 
Arun Narayan: 
Yes, yes, go ahead. 

 
 
Titan Company Limited
 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 9 of 17 
Sensitivity: Internal
Jay Doshi: 
Sorry, I will get back in the queue. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Nihal Mahesh Jham from HSBC. Please go ahead. 
Nihal Mahesh Jham: 
Yes. Hi, team. Good evening. I had two questions. The first was on TMZ. Our buyer growth was 
5% in Q1. We have seen it obviously become flat. Just wanted to understand, is it because of the 
festive shift or the gold coin, or your comments on it? 
Arun Narayan: 
Both of that, Nihal. Both the festive shift as well as the gold coin and investment buying, both 
have contributed. 
Nihal Mahesh Jham: 
And has that then improved in the overall festive season in terms of buyer growth turning 
positive? 
Arun Narayan: 
Yes. I will say it is better than that, but a lot depends on these last few days. I hope I can say that 
at the end of festive period. Do wish us luck on that. 
Nihal Mahesh Jham: 
No, sure will. The second question was that you have obviously seen the recent trends in terms 
of gold prices sort of being moderate, and generally, we have always had this belief that 
customers come in with a certain budget when they buy jewellery. 
 
As gold has sort of corrected, how are the bill values for customers sort of reacting? Are they up 
trending in terms of number of pieces? Are they buying higher weightage jewellery? How is the 
bill value sort of reacting to the customers that are entering this? 
Arun Narayan: 
Actually, this has been a recent phenomenon during the festive period. Perhaps once it is over, 
we will kind of get into it, and possibly answer you with greater accuracy. Because during the 
festive, it is kind of a rush at this time, so we may not have analysed that to answer your question 
with the depth that it requires. 
Nihal Mahesh Jham: 
I hear you. That was it from my side. Wish you all the best and happy Diwali. 
Arun Narayan: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Amit Purohit from Elara Capital. Please go ahead. 
Amit Purohit: 
Hi, Sir. Thank you for the opportunity. Just continuing on the buyer growth itself, I just wanted 
to understand between the studded, which has been growing pretty strong for us for the last 
couple of quarters, I wanted to understand the consumer behaviour more, to put it in a way that 
if the buyer comes in, does the new buyer growth directly happens in the studded segment, or 
he goes through a life cycle kind of a, that he first buys a plain gold jewellery and that gets into 
a studded? What has been your experience for it? Because we have been actually launching a lot 
of new products. Zoya has been pushed, so a lot of studded products I see that launches has been 
there. 

 
 
Titan Company Limited
 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 10 of 17 
Sensitivity: Internal
Arun Narayan: 
Actually, it's a mix of both, Amit. Like Ajoy said, a lot of younger customers come in and make 
their first purchase as a diamond product, and it's across all three brands, Tanishq, Mia, and 
CaratLane. But we do find a lot of traditional gold buyers also moving over to diamonds after 
having bought gold over a period of time, who tend to be slightly older customers. So, we see 
both happening. But perhaps in a CaratLane store or a Mia store, a lot of the customers are first-
time diamond buyers. In Tanishq, it's a mix of the two. 
Amit Purohit: 
Okay. Just a follow-up on this. So, last quarter growth, say, 30% in the studded business, there 
would be buyer growth in that segment, or in the Tanishq part of the portfolio, or it is difficult 
to right now understand that. Over the last six months or so, the studded portion has been strong 
in the Tanishq part of the portfolio. Is it a fair assumption that buyer growth could be slightly 
higher in that versus… 
Arun Narayan: 
Yes. Buyer growth is certainly higher in that segment. 
Amit Purohit: 
Okay. Thanks a lot, sir. Thank you, and all the best, and wish you a happy Diwali. 
Arun Narayan: 
Thank you. You too. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Avi Mehta from 360 ONE Capital. Please go ahead. 
Avi Mehta: 
Yes. Hi, team. Thanks a lot for the opportunity. Just first question on the entry-level segment. I 
am not sure if it was covered, sorry for that. If you could give us a sense on whether there has 
been a change in that behaviour where we were seeing demand kind of being a little muted, if 
that has changed because of the gold price correction. 
 
If you could kind of help us with that. Also, if the buyer growth, how should we look at buyer 
growth when we are because as you rightly pointed out, we should look at it ex-gold coins. Buyer 
growth may not be the right factor then. Do you think EBIT growth is the right factor? If you 
could kind of help us understand how do you look at this internally. Thank you. 
Arun Narayan: 
No, from an operations standpoint, we will obviously look at it as a core jewellery growth, 
because that is our primary focus. Pure core jewellery growth in buyer terms and in value terms, 
that is the way that we look at it. The gold rate softening is a very recent piece, Avi, so we will 
also need some time to step back and see what has been the result of that. 
 
So do allow us some time to answer that question after the end of festive. But the trend that you 
allude to has been true in the last couple of quarters and prior to that as gold rates have been 
increasing. 
Ajoy Chawla: 
Sir, I will just step in. There are quite a few questions coming from many of you saying, "How 
should we think about growth going forward given gold prices have corrected?" So, If I were to 
take a shot at it, I would say that if gold prices remain corrected and stable, the chances are we 
will see many more customers coming into the market, especially those who had stayed away. 

 
 
Titan Company Limited
 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 11 of 17 
Sensitivity: Internal
 
And therefore, I would bet on much healthier buyer growth than what we have seen in the past, 
perhaps compensating for some of the ticket size-related issues that you might be anticipating 
because gold prices remain subdued. The second piece I would say is new buyers, I don't think 
we should think about it as studded or gold. You didn't ask for this, but the previous gentleman 
asked for it.

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to BSE Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. As a 
reminder, all participants will be in the listen only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask 
questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, 
please signal an operator by pressing star then zero and you touch tone phone. Please note that this

I now hand the conference over to Mr. Anand Sethuraman. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Anand Sethuraman: 
 
Thank you so much, Yusuf. Good evening, everyone. Welcome to BSE's Q2 FY 2027 Earnings Call. I'm 
Anand Sethuraman, and it's my privilege to introduce you to the members of the BSE's leadership team 
today. 
Starting with Mr. Sundararaman Ramamurthy, Managing Director and CEO; Mr. Saurabh Shukla and Mr. 
Gopalan S. Raghavan, Executive Directors; Mr. Deepak Goel, Chief Financial Officer; Mr. Sunil 
Ramrakhiani, Chief Business Officer; Ms Geetha Gangadharan, Chief Regulatory Officer; Mr. Viral 
Davda, Chief Technology Officer; Mr. Rudresh Kunde, Chief of Product, Policy and Strategy, Ms. Radha 
Kirthivasan, Head of Issuer Relations and Corporate Sales; Mr. Ramesh Gurram, Chief Information 
Security Officer; Mr. Abhishek Jha, Joint Chief Information Security Officer; Mr. Sanjay Jain, Chief Risk 
Officer; Mr. Vishal Bhat, Company Secretary; Mr. Ashutosh Singh, Managing Director and CEO, BSE 
Index Services; Ms. Vaishali Babu, Managing Director and CEO of BSE Clearing Corporation. We also 
have representatives from our finance, business, Investor Relations team here. 
Please note that our latest financial results and investor presentation are available on the BSE website. 
Today, we'll start with remarks from our MD and CEO on our performance, followed by a Q&A session. 
All participant lines will be muted for the duration of the call and there will be an opportunity for you to 
ask questions after the management remarks. Some of the remarks made today in this call may be 
forward-looking in nature and are subject to risks and uncertainties. The company does not undertake 
to update these forward-looking statements publicly. 
With that, I would now invite BSE MD and CEO to share his views. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 

ESSE 
The Power of Vibrance 
 
2 
 
BSE - PUBLIC
S. Ramamurthy: 
Thank you. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Let me begin by welcoming our 
shareholders, analysts, investors, members and all other stakeholders on this call. Let me first talk a 
little bit about the macroeconomic environment. Indian capital markets continue to demonstrate 
structural resilience despite a volatile global environment marked by intensifying geopolitical tensions, 
fluctuating crude oil prices and prolonged tightening of global financial conditions. 
Against this challenging backdrop, India's core macroeconomic fundamentals remain exceptionally 
robust. Real GDP expanded by 7.8% in Q1 of FY27, fundamentally driven by sustained momentum 
across private consumption, capital investment, manufacturing output and a resurgent services sector. 
Importantly, institutional market dynamics have evolved to provide unparalleled systemic stability. 
While foreign institutional investors adopted a cautious stance amid macro uncertainties resulting in a 
net outflow of approximately Rs. 35,861 crores from Indian equities in September 2026 domestic 
institutional investors absorbed this liquidity pressure, deploying approximately Rs. 76,030 crores 
during the same period. 
This robust influx of domestic capital serves as a critical countercyclical buffer, deepening market 
liquidity and validating long-term confidence in the Indian growth narrative. Indian capital markets are 
now increasingly anchored by domestic long-term financial savings. 
Evidencing this depth, the mutual fund industry's assets under management reached a historic 
milestone of approximately Rs. 82.64 lakh crores as of September 2026, making an impressive 12.5% 
expansion during the first half of FY27. The compounding participation of both household and 
institutional investors underscores the self-sustaining nature, maturation and expanding capacity of the 
domestic financial ecosystem. 
Against this backdrop, I'm pleased to share that BSE continued to deliver strong financial performance 
during the first half of FY27. Consolidated revenues for H1 FY27 stood at Rs. 3,257 crores compared 
with Rs. 2,184 crores in the corresponding period last year, representing a robust year-on-year growth 
of 49%. 
I will now share some of the key financial numbers on a consolidated basis for the half year ended 
September 30, 2026, as compared to the previous year. Operational revenues have grown by 48% to 
Rs. 2,999 crores from Rs. 2,026 crores. 

ESSE 
The Power of Vibrance 
 
3 
 
BSE - PUBLIC
Transaction charges comprising revenues from the equity cash, equity derivatives, mutual fund and 
clearing house segments registered a substantial increase of 60%, rising to Rs. 2,456 crores from Rs. 
1,531 crores reflecting robust growth in core trading and settlement related activities. Other operating 
income, which includes enhanced data dissemination fees, co-location and order throttle charges, 
index services, etc., has increased by 23% to Rs. 200 crores from Rs. 163 crores. Operating expenses 
increased by 36% Rs. 980 crores from Rs. 721 crores. It may be noted that 50% of the total operating 
expenses are attributable to regulatory fees and clearing and settlement expenses, all of which is 
directly correlated to increasing transaction volumes. The operating EBITDA, including contribution to 
core SGF has increased by 55% to Rs. 2,019 crores as compared to Rs. 1,306 crores with margins 
expanding to 67% from 64%. 
The net profit attributable to the shareholders of the company has demonstrated a significant increase 
to reach Rs. 1,680 crores from Rs. 1,095 crores representing a robust year-on-year growth of 53% with 
a net profit margin of 52%. The continued growth of BSE's investor base remains an encouraging 
indicator of the growing reach of India's capital markets. Investor accounts registered on BSE have now 
reached 26.8 crores, 3.9 crores new accounts added over the past year. 
Importantly, this participation is becoming increasingly broad-based with 11 states now having more 
than 1 crore investor reach, reflecting the widening geographic reach of the capital markets across the 
country. 
Alongside this growth, investor education and awareness continue to remain an important priority for 
BSE. We conducted 2,328 investor awareness programs during H1 FY27 reaching over 1.2 lakhs 
participants. Looking ahead, BSE remains deeply committed to expanding investor awareness and 
advancing financial literacy. 
We view this educational mandate as a key pillar for promoting informed investment decision 
safeguarding investor interest and securing the long-term sustainable growth of India's financial 
ecosystem. The consistent improvement across both our revenue streams and operating margins is 
direct evidence of our disciplined strategic execution. By expanding market participation and driving key 
platform efficiencies, we are continuously enhancing the depth of India's financial ecosystem while 
reinforcing BSE's structural position at the center of India's capital market expansion. 

ESSE

4 
 
BSE - PUBLIC
Let me now discuss a few key trends that shaped our business this quarter. In primary markets, we have 
seen very strong momentum during the first half of FY27 with a record 71 main board IPOs, raising over 
Rs. 84,000 crores, making it the strongest on record for Indian capital markets. 
In September alone, BSE witnessed a record 32 main board IPO listings, collectively raising Rs. 40,354 
crores. The strong pipeline of issuances coupled with healthy investor participation demonstrates the 
growing confidence of companies in accessing the public markets for capital formation. 
We remain optimistic about the opportunities ahead and believe BSE is well positioned to participate in 
India's growing equity capital markets. Alongside the strong momentum in the main board IPO market, 
the SME segment also continued to demonstrate healthy growth with strong issuer and investor 
participation. 
BSE SME crossed a significant milestone of 800 listed companies in October 2026, up from 600 a year 
earlier. Notably, the latest 200 listings have raised Rs. 8,387 crores representing nearly 45% of the 
cumulative capital raised on the platform, underscoring the growing role of SMEs in India's economic 
growth and capital market development. 
Overall, in H1 FY 2027, issuers raised over Rs. 13.9 lakh crores through BSE's fundraising platforms 
across equity, debt, bonds, commercial papers, REITS, and InvITs, reaffirming the trust placed in BSE's 
market infrastructure. Looking ahead, we remain positive on the outlook for India's primary markets. 
The main board IPO pipeline remains strong, with over 150 companies seeking to access the capital 
markets and targeting fund raising of approximately Rs. 1.5 lakh crores. Moving on to our trading 
segment. 
We continue to witness strong momentum across both our cash and derivatives market, supported by 
growing client participation and product innovation. In the equity cash segment, BSE continued its 
strong momentum, recording its highest ever quarterly average daily turnover of Rs. 10,494 crores in Q2 
FY27 reflecting sustained market participation and strengthening liquidity on the exchange. 
In our Index options segment, Q2 FY27 ADTV by premium volumes stood at Rs. 22,531 crores. While 
this represents our first sequential quarterly contraction decreasing from Rs. 29,615 crores in Q1 due 
to compressed market volatility and certain temporary structural shifts in participation.

Rationale 
ICRA has withdrawn the rating assigned to the bank facilities of Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), at the request of the 
company, based on the No Objection Certificates (NOC) received from its bankers, and in accordance with ICRA’s policy on 
withdrawal of credit ratings. However, ICRA does not have information to suggest that the credit risk has changed since the 
time the rating was last reviewed. 
The key rating drivers and their description, liquidity position and rating sensitivities have not been captured as the rated 
instruments are being withdrawn. The previous detailed rating rationale is available at the following link: Click here.

HAL holds for the GoI in defence sector, which we expect should induce it to extend timely 
financial support to the rated entity, should there be a need.

About the Company 
HAL, a defence public sector undertaking (DPSU), was established on October 1, 1964, with the amalgamation of Hindustan 
Aircraft Limited and Aeronautics India Limited. The principal business of HAL is to undertake design, development, 
manufacturing, maintenance, repair, overhaul, and servicing of aircraft, helicopters, engines and other related systems like 
avionics, instruments, and accessories. Its primary consumers are the Indian defence forces comprising the Indian Air Force, 
Indian Army, Indian Navy and the Indian Coast Guard. It also engages with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) to 
contribute to its space programmes. The GoI remains HAL’s largest shareholder, with a stake of 71.64% as on March 31, 2026. 
HAL was conferred with the Navratna PSU status in June 2007 and Maharatna status in October 2024. The board of directors 
also include two nominee directors from the GoI.

withdrawal of credit ratings. However, ICRA does not have information to suggest that the credit risk has changed since the

About the Company 
HAL, a defence public sector undertaking (DPSU), was established on October 1, 1964, with the amalgamation of Hindustan 
Aircraft Limited and Aeronautics India Limited. The principal business of HAL is to undertake design, development, 
manufacturing, maintenance, repair, overhaul, and servicing of aircraft, helicopters, engines and other related systems like 
avionics, instruments, and accessories. Its primary consumers are the Indian defence forces comprising the Indian Air Force, 
Indian Army, Indian Navy and the Indian Coast Guard. It also engages with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) to 
contribute to its space programmes. The GoI remains HAL’s largest shareholder, with a stake of 71.64% as on March 31, 2026. 
HAL was conferred with the Navratna PSU status in June 2007 and Maharatna status in October 2024. The board of directors 
also include two nominee directors from the GoI.

TVS MOTOR EXPANDS ITS GLOBAL PORTFOLIO 
WITH TVS CALLISTO 110 LAUNCH IN ISTANBUL 
• 
Features longest seat in the segment, increased legroom, 12-inch alloy wheels, three-
step adjustable rear shock absorbers  
• 
It also offers a 33-litre under-seat storage, front-facing fuel filling, an all-in-one lock 
system and a glove box with mobile charging 
 
Singapore/Istanbul, November 11, 2026: TVS Motor Company (TVSM), part of TVS VENU, and a 
reputed global manufacturer of two and three-wheelers, today launched the TVS Callisto 110 in Istanbul 
in partnership with Uğur Motorlu Araçlar. The launch event brought together over 50 attendees, 
including automobile enthusiasts and representatives from TVS Motor Company and UMA.  
This global product is well-suited to the mobility options needed in Istanbul that make everyday rides 
more convenient. With this launch, TVS Callisto will offer customers the convenience of automatic 
transmission, fuel-efficiency-focused technology and practical features that will support everyday urban 
travel. The launch further expands the company’s international portfolio, bringing a scooter designed 
for everyday commutes that is built for real-world mobility. 
The TVS Callisto is powered by a 113.3 cc, fuel-injected engine paired with a CVTi automatic 
transmission. Its Integrated Starter Generator enables silent starting, while the next-generation Stop-
Go technology is designed to improve fuel efficiency by switching off the engine during brief stops, 
improving fuel-efficiency by 10%.  
Designed to enhance rider and passenger comfort, the scooter features a longest seat in the segment, 
increased legroom, 12-inch alloy wheels, three-step adjustable rear shock absorbers and Body Balance 
Technology and signature infinity head & tail lamp. It also offers a 33-litre under-seat storage 
compartment capable of accommodating two half-face helmets, front-facing fuel filling, an all-in-one 
lock system and a glove box with mobile charging. 
Commenting on the Turkey launch, Peyman Kargar, President, International Business, TVS Motor 
Company, said, “Türkiye is an important market in our international growth journey and we are pleased 
to introduce the TVS Callisto. The product has been developed around the needs of everyday urban 
riders, bringing together refined performance, comfort and relevant modern design. As we continue to 
expand our global footprint, we remain committed to strengthening our engagement with customers 
while building a sustainable foundation for long-term growth in the region.” 
With a modern design and a variety of first-in-segment features, TVS Callisto is tailored to offer the best 
of technology and safety features, including a metal body, Follow Me Headlamp, hazard lamps, 
automatic turn-signal reset and Emergency Brake Warning. It also features a fully digital colored 
instrument cluster with connected functions such as Bluetooth connectivity, navigation & voice 
assistance and call & text notifications.  
The TVS Callisto 110 will be available in three attractive colour options: Blue, White and Red, at a 
starting price of ₺ 132,600.  
 

 
 
 
About TVS Motor Company 
 
TVS Motor Company (BSE:532343 and NSE: TVSMOTOR), part of TVS VENU, is a reputed two and 
three-wheeler manufacturer globally, championing progress through sustainable mobility with four 
state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities located in India and Indonesia. Rooted in our 100-year legacy 
of trust, value, and passion for customers, it takes pride in making internationally accepted products of 
the highest quality through innovative and sustainable processes. TVS Motor is the only two-wheeler 
company to have won the prestigious Deming Prize. Our products lead in their respective categories in 
the J.D. Power IQS and APEAL surveys. We have been ranked No. 1 Company in the J.D. Power 
Customer Service Satisfaction Survey for four consecutive years. Our group company Norton 
Motorcycles, based in the United Kingdom, is one of the most emotive motorcycle brands in the world. 
TVS Motor Company endeavors to deliver the most superior customer experience across 90 countries 
in which we operate.  
 
For more information, please visit www.tvsmotor.com

Singapore/Istanbul, November 11, 2026: TVS Motor Company (TVSM), part of TVS VENU, and a 
reputed global manufacturer of two and three-wheelers, today launched the TVS Callisto 110 in Istanbul 
in partnership with Uğur Motorlu Araçlar. The launch event brought together over 50 attendees, 
including automobile enthusiasts and representatives from TVS Motor Company and UMA.  
This global product is well-suited to the mobility options needed in Istanbul that make everyday rides 
more convenient. With this launch, TVS Callisto will offer customers the convenience of automatic 
transmission, fuel-efficiency-focused technology and practical features that will support everyday urban 
travel. The launch further expands the company’s international portfolio, bringing a scooter designed 
for everyday commutes that is built for real-world mobility. 
The TVS Callisto is powered by a 113.3 cc, fuel-injected engine paired with a CVTi automatic 
transmission. Its Integrated Starter Generator enables silent starting, while the next-generation Stop-
Go technology is designed to improve fuel efficiency by switching off the engine during brief stops, 
improving fuel-efficiency by 10%.  
Designed to enhance rider and passenger comfort, the scooter features a longest seat in the segment, 
increased legroom, 12-inch alloy wheels, three-step adjustable rear shock absorbers and Body Balance 
Technology and signature infinity head & tail lamp. It also offers a 33-litre under-seat storage 
compartment capable of accommodating two half-face helmets, front-facing fuel filling, an all-in-one 
lock system and a glove box with mobile charging. 
Commenting on the Turkey launch, Peyman Kargar, President, International Business, TVS Motor 
Company, said, “Türkiye is an important market in our international growth journey and we are pleased 
to introduce the TVS Callisto. The product has been developed around the needs of everyday urban 
riders, bringing together refined performance, comfort and relevant modern design. As we continue to 
expand our global footprint, we remain committed to strengthening our engagement with customers 
while building a sustainable foundation for long-term growth in the region.” 
With a modern design and a variety of first-in-segment features, TVS Callisto is tailored to offer the best 
of technology and safety features, including a metal body, Follow Me Headlamp, hazard lamps, 
automatic turn-signal reset and Emergency Brake Warning. It also features a fully digital colored 
instrument cluster with connected functions such as Bluetooth connectivity, navigation & voice 
assistance and call & text notifications.  
The TVS Callisto 110 will be available in three attractive colour options: Blue, White and Red, at a 
starting price of ₺ 132,600.  
 

 
 
 
About TVS Motor Company 
 
TVS Motor Company (BSE:532343 and NSE: TVSMOTOR), part of TVS VENU, is a reputed two and 
three-wheeler manufacturer globally, championing progress through sustainable mobility with four 
state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities located in India and Indonesia. Rooted in our 100-year legacy 
of trust, value, and passion for customers, it takes pride in making internationally accepted products of 
the highest quality through innovative and sustainable processes. TVS Motor is the only two-wheeler 
company to have won the prestigious Deming Prize. Our products lead in their respective categories in 
the J.D. Power IQS and APEAL surveys. We have been ranked No. 1 Company in the J.D. Power 
Customer Service Satisfaction Survey for four consecutive years. Our group company Norton 
Motorcycles, based in the United Kingdom, is one of the most emotive motorcycle brands in the world. 
TVS Motor Company endeavors to deliver the most superior customer experience across 90 countries 
in which we operate.

in ‘Listen-only’ mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after

Varun Mali: Thank you, Vandit. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to our 2nd

release that was sent out yesterday. These are also available on our website. 
 
I would now like to introduce our senior management team who is on the call with us today, 
represented by: 
 
• Dr. Satakarni Makkapati, CEO - Aurobindo Biosimilars, Vaccines, Peptides Businesses 
and Director - Aurobindo Pharma Limited.

• Mr. V. Muralidharan, CEO, Europe Formulations Business. 
• Mr. S. Subramanian, CFO, Aurobindo Pharma Limited. 
 
We will begin the call with the summary highlights from the management followed by an 
interactive Q&A session. Please note that some of the matters we will discuss today are 
forward-looking, including and without limitations, statements relating to the 
implementation of strategic actions and other affirmations on our future business, business 
development and commercial performance. While these forward-looking statements 
exemplify a judgment and future expectations concerning the development of a business, a 
number of risks, uncertainties, and other important factors which may cause developments 
and results to vary materially from our expectations. Aurobindo Pharma undertakes no 
obligation to publicly revise any forward-looking statements to reflect in future events or 
circumstances. 
 
With that, I will now hand over the call to our CFO for the business highlights. Over to you, 
Sir. 
 
S. Subramanian: Good morning, everyone. Welcome to Aurobindo Pharma Q2 FY27 earnings 
call. Thank you for joining us. Today, we will take you through our performance for the 
quarter, along with the strategic priorities that we believe will shape the Aurobindo’s next 
phase of growth. We are working to translate the scale of the established business, strength 
of our development pipeline and the capacities created through recent investment into 
sustainable commercial growth. 
 
Key objective highlights for the quarter: We completed the acquisition of Lannett, further 
strengthening our US presence and expanding our capabilities in complex and controlled

substances. The acquisition provides opportunities to enhance our product portfolio, leverage 
our existing commercial capabilities and drive incremental growth. The A1 Biochem 
acquisition makes an important step towards establishing an integrated, end-to-end small 
molecule CRDMO business, with capability spanning the value chain and experience of 
handling the development portfolio of more than 800 projects. We launched ADQUEY, our 
first new chemical entity / NDA product for atopic dermatitis, alongside the launch of the 
dedicated dermatology business and unit focused on developing and commercializing high-
value dermatology products. The launch of key products such as generic Advair and the 
approval of generic QVAR marked the milestones in our expansion into the high-value 
respiratory segment, leveraging our capabilities in complex inhalation products. The Raleigh 
unit recently received a VAI classification, supporting the regulatory pathway for additional 
filings and approval in transdermal, dermal and respiratory products, and reinforcing our 
plans to expand in these differentiated segments. 
 
Business performance: We are pleased to report our highest ever revenue for the quarter of 
10,263 crores, representing year-on-year growth of 24%. This performance reflects 
contribution from our core market, successful integration and continued progress across our 
strategic growth priority.  
 
Operating EBITDA was 2,156 crores, growing at 28% year-on-year with a margin of 21%, 
despite increase in input cost and freight rate. Our focus remains on sustained profitability 
through product mix improvement, manufacturing efficiencies and disciplined spending and 
better utilization of our assets. 
 
Formulation generated revenue of 9,102 crores, growing 24% year-on-year and accounting 
for approximately 89% of the consolidated revenue. Our Formulation franchise continues to 
benefit from its geographical breadth, product diversity and ability to compete across a range 
of market segments.  
 
API revenue stood at 1,162 crores, growing 21% year-on-year and contributing approximately 
11% of the overall revenue. In addition to this direct contribution, API business supports the 
reliability, competitiveness and integration of our broader manufacturing model. 
 
In the US, revenue was 4,555 crores, equivalent to USD 477 million, reflecting growth of 25% 
year-on-year. Our focus remains on maximizing the potential of our established portfolio, 
while accelerating the launch of complex and differentiated products, which are expected to 
contribute increasingly to our growth and product mix. During the quarter, we launched 10 
products in the US, filed 7 ANDAs and received 12 final approvals.  
 
Europe delivered revenue of €288 million, with constant currency growth of 18%. We 
continue to build on our established market presence, product portfolio and operating 
capabilities. Revenue from growth market is 1,026 crores or USD 107 million, representing 
year-on-year growth of 16%. Our approach is to deepen market presence, broaden access to 
our portfolio and sustain momentum across the priority geography. ARV formulation was $38 
million during the quarter, supported by stable volume.

Profitability, investments and financial position: Gross margin for the quarter was 61.2% 
compared to 59.7% in the corresponding period last year, while contribution stood at 6,280 
crores. We continue to focus on product mix and procurement discipline and operating 
efficiency as levers to strengthen profitability.  
 
Total capital expenditure stood at 89 million, of which 47 million towards the development 
capabilities and 42 million towards strategic priorities respectively, thereby supporting our 
future growth plan.  
 
R&D expenditure for the quarter stood at 376 crores against INR 344 crores in previous 
quarter. Our development investments are directed towards advancing differentiated 
products and building a pipeline with meaningful long-term commercial potential. 
 
We have generated a very strong cash flow of USD 146 million during the quarter after funding 
strategic investments and capital allocation initiatives, and closed with a net cash position of 
USD 189 million. Our balance sheet provides a sound foundation to support planned 
investment while preserving financial flexibility.  
 
Average finance cost of 4.9%, and profit after tax for the quarter was 1,124 crores. Going 
forward, our focus will be continuously improving capacity utilization, enhancing product mix, 
driving manufacturing efficiencies and maintaining tight working capital discipline. 
 
Outlook: Our growth strategy is supported by key drivers, each with different distinct 
commercial pathways that collectively diversify our sources of growth and reduce reliance on 
any single product.  
 
Strengthening and monetizing our US business: In the US, Lannett acquisition has broadened 
our presence in complex and controlled substance. The focus is now on effective integration, 
portfolio development and leveraging our established commercial and manufacturing 
capabilities to capture the value of the asset.  
 
Expanding our differentiated product portfolio: Complex generics remain the central to our 
strategy of moving towards a more differentiated product. Respiratory therapy, including dry 
powder inhalers and metered-dose inhalers, represent an important opportunity. The recent 
approvals and launches demonstrate progress in this area. Our focus is on advancing 
regulatory milestone, converting development work into launches and building a sustainable 
portfolio in technically demanding category. 
 
Biosimilars and specialty products represent important opportunities to strengthen our 
presence in complex and high-value segments. We remain focused on advancing our pipeline, 
building commercial capabilities and pursuing opportunities that offer strong market 
potential and attractive long-term return. 
CDMO focus: The A1 Biochem acquisition marks a significant step towards building an 
integrated, end-to-end small molecules CRDMO business. In parallel, Lannett manufacturing 
capabilities, including around 70 commercial product families, provide opportunities to 
expand CDMO offering, deepen customer relation and diversify sources of growth. Our focus

will be on converting the development pipeline and available capacities into sustainable 
customer programs and commercial outlook.  
 
Additionally, our biologics contract manufacturing business provide another avenue for 
growth, complementing our capabilities and broadening the overall service offering, 
improving utilization and leveraging integration. 
 
Our China oral solid dosage facility is entering into a phase where execution and capacity 
utilization become increasingly important. As supplies to international market expand, our 
focus will be on customer conversion, consistent delivery and scaling production into 
commercially disciplined manner.  
 
Our API and backward integration capabilities remain an important competitive advantage, 
strengthening the supply security, ensuring quality and cost competitiveness. We continue to 
leverage these capabilities to drive operational efficiencies, improve cost structures and 
enhance overall business competitiveness. 
 
Capital productivity: We will continue to maintain a disciplined approach to capital allocation 
and balancing investments with the objective of generating sustainable cash flows and 
improving returns on capital employed. Strong working capital management and operating 
efficiency and balance sheet discipline will be a key priority. Our long-term ambition is to build 
a business with a higher share of differentiated products, multiple sustainable growth drivers, 
and then improving return profile. We believe our established scale, combined with the 
increasing contribution from newer businesses, will position us to deliver sustainable growth 
and long-term shareholder value. 
 
FY27 guidance: For the remainder of the financial year, our focus will be on sustaining 
execution across our core businesses while accelerating progress across our strategic 
initiatives. We reiterate our FY guidance with the double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA 
margins north of 21% and absolute EBITDA in excess of 8,000 crore, with a potential upside

confident in our ability to further expand our EBITDA margin to upwards of 22% in the coming

strategic growth drivers.

• Mr. S. Subramanian, CFO, Aurobindo Pharma Limited. 
 
We will begin the call with the summary highlights from the management followed by an 
interactive Q&A session. Please note that some of the matters we will discuss today are 
forward-looking, including and without limitations, statements relating to the 
implementation of strategic actions and other affirmations on our future business, business 
development and commercial performance. While these forward-looking statements 
exemplify a judgment and future expectations concerning the development of a business, a 
number of risks, uncertainties, and other important factors which may cause developments 
and results to vary materially from our expectations. Aurobindo Pharma undertakes no 
obligation to publicly revise any forward-looking statements to reflect in future events or 
circumstances. 
 
With that, I will now hand over the call to our CFO for the business highlights. Over to you, 
Sir. 
 
S. Subramanian: Good morning, everyone. Welcome to Aurobindo Pharma Q2 FY27 earnings 
call. Thank you for joining us. Today, we will take you through our performance for the 
quarter, along with the strategic priorities that we believe will shape the Aurobindo’s next 
phase of growth. We are working to translate the scale of the established business, strength 
of our development pipeline and the capacities created through recent investment into 
sustainable commercial growth. 
 
Key objective highlights for the quarter: We completed the acquisition of Lannett, further 
strengthening our US presence and expanding our capabilities in complex and controlled

substances. The acquisition provides opportunities to enhance our product portfolio, leverage 
our existing commercial capabilities and drive incremental growth. The A1 Biochem 
acquisition makes an important step towards establishing an integrated, end-to-end small 
molecule CRDMO business, with capability spanning the value chain and experience of 
handling the development portfolio of more than 800 projects. We launched ADQUEY, our 
first new chemical entity / NDA product for atopic dermatitis, alongside the launch of the 
dedicated dermatology business and unit focused on developing and commercializing high-
value dermatology products. The launch of key products such as generic Advair and the 
approval of generic QVAR marked the milestones in our expansion into the high-value 
respiratory segment, leveraging our capabilities in complex inhalation products. The Raleigh 
unit recently received a VAI classification, supporting the regulatory pathway for additional 
filings and approval in transdermal, dermal and respiratory products, and reinforcing our 
plans to expand in these differentiated segments. 
 
Business performance: We are pleased to report our highest ever revenue for the quarter of 
10,263 crores, representing year-on-year growth of 24%. This performance reflects 
contribution from our core market, successful integration and continued progress across our 
strategic growth priority.  
 
Operating EBITDA was 2,156 crores, growing at 28% year-on-year with a margin of 21%, 
despite increase in input cost and freight rate. Our focus remains on sustained profitability 
through product mix improvement, manufacturing efficiencies and disciplined spending and 
better utilization of our assets. 
 
Formulation generated revenue of 9,102 crores, growing 24% year-on-year and accounting 
for approximately 89% of the consolidated revenue. Our Formulation franchise continues to 
benefit from its geographical breadth, product diversity and ability to compete across a range 
of market segments.  
 
API revenue stood at 1,162 crores, growing 21% year-on-year and contributing approximately 
11% of the overall revenue. In addition to this direct contribution, API business supports the 
reliability, competitiveness and integration of our broader manufacturing model. 
 
In the US, revenue was 4,555 crores, equivalent to USD 477 million, reflecting growth of 25% 
year-on-year. Our focus remains on maximizing the potential of our established portfolio, 
while accelerating the launch of complex and differentiated products, which are expected to 
contribute increasingly to our growth and product mix. During the quarter, we launched 10 
products in the US, filed 7 ANDAs and received 12 final approvals.  
 
Europe delivered revenue of €288 million, with constant currency growth of 18%. We 
continue to build on our established market presence, product portfolio and operating 
capabilities. Revenue from growth market is 1,026 crores or USD 107 million, representing 
year-on-year growth of 16%. Our approach is to deepen market presence, broaden access to 
our portfolio and sustain momentum across the priority geography. ARV formulation was $38 
million during the quarter, supported by stable volume.

Profitability, investments and financial position: Gross margin for the quarter was 61.2% 
compared to 59.7% in the corresponding period last year, while contribution stood at 6,280 
crores. We continue to focus on product mix and procurement discipline and operating 
efficiency as levers to strengthen profitability.  
 
Total capital expenditure stood at 89 million, of which 47 million towards the development 
capabilities and 42 million towards strategic priorities respectively, thereby supporting our 
future growth plan.  
 
R&D expenditure for the quarter stood at 376 crores against INR 344 crores in previous 
quarter. Our development investments are directed towards advancing differentiated 
products and building a pipeline with meaningful long-term commercial potential. 
 
We have generated a very strong cash flow of USD 146 million during the quarter after funding 
strategic investments and capital allocation initiatives, and closed with a net cash position of 
USD 189 million. Our balance sheet provides a sound foundation to support planned 
investment while preserving financial flexibility.  
 
Average finance cost of 4.9%, and profit after tax for the quarter was 1,124 crores. Going 
forward, our focus will be continuously improving capacity utilization, enhancing product mix, 
driving manufacturing efficiencies and maintaining tight working capital discipline.

commercial pathways that collectively diversify our sources of growth and reduce reliance on 
any single product.

our presence in complex and controlled substance. The focus is now on effective integration, 
portfolio development and leveraging our established commercial and manufacturing 
capabilities to capture the value of the asset.  
 
Expanding our differentiated product portfolio: Complex generics remain the central to our 
strategy of moving towards a more differentiated product. Respiratory therapy, including dry 
powder inhalers and metered-dose inhalers, represent an important opportunity. The recent 
approvals and launches demonstrate progress in this area. Our focus is on advancing 
regulatory milestone, converting development work into launches and building a sustainable 
portfolio in technically demanding category. 
 
Biosimilars and specialty products represent important opportunities to strengthen our 
presence in complex and high-value segments. We remain focused on advancing our pipeline, 
building commercial capabilities and pursuing opportunities that offer strong market 
potential and attractive long-term return. 
CDMO focus: The A1 Biochem acquisition marks a significant step towards building an 
integrated, end-to-end small molecules CRDMO business. In parallel, Lannett manufacturing 
capabilities, including around 70 commercial product families, provide opportunities to 
expand CDMO offering, deepen customer relation and diversify sources of growth. Our focus

Press Release 
 
 
Rampur Indian Single Malt Unveils A Natural Brand Positioning, ‘43° | 2° – Born in 
Nature’s Frequency’ 
The only Indian whisky selected for The 8 Continent Series, an international study of how 
climate shapes single malt 
New Delhi, November 11, 2026 – Rampur Indian Single Malt, the globally acclaimed Indian single 
malt from Radico Khaitan Limited, has unveiled, ‘43° | 2° – Born in Nature’s Frequency’, a new brand 
positioning built on the two temperature extremes of its home in the Himalayan foothills, 43°C in 
summer and 2°C in winter. This seasonal swing, which expands and contracts the oak cask year after 
year, shapes the character of the whisky. As Rampur completes its first decade, it now becomes the 
signature of the brand. 
The influence of this climate is also the subject of international scientific research. Rampur Distillery 
has been selected to represent Asia in The 8 Continent Series, a six-month study examining how 
geographical and climatic conditions influence the maturation, chemistry and flavour of single malt 
whisky. Led by Brazilian food scientist Aline Bortoletto and her team at INOVBEV, the study brings 
together eight single malts from different continents, including one matured in Antarctica, and will use 
chemical analysis, sensory evaluation and statistical modelling to understand the influence of 
climate on whisky. Rampur is the only Indian whisky in the study, bringing the conditions of the 
Himalayan foothills into a global conversation on whisky maturation. 
Since its launch in 2016, Rampur has built its identity around the character imparted by its place of 
origin. The natural positioning brings this provenance into sharper focus. The campaign line, ‘Born in 
Nature’s Frequency’, connects the rhythm of the natural world with the maturation process. Heat 
expands the cask, cold contracts it, and the spirit gradually develops its character. Read together, 43 
and 2 form 432, which now serves as Rampur’s numerical signature. The platform makes visible a 
process that is largely unseen, giving consumers a new way to understand the relationship between 
Rampur’s provenance and the whisky in the glass. 
Kunal Madan, Chief Marketing Officer, Radico Khaitan, said, “Over the past decade, Rampur has 
established a distinct identity in the world of Indian single malts, earning recognition internationally 
while remaining deeply connected to its place of origin. In a climate as demanding as ours, the cask 
works through every season, and we wanted a platform that places this truth at the heart of the brand. 
‘43° | 2° – Born in Nature’s Frequency’ brings together the climate, the craft and the character of the 
whisky. The number 432 also carries cultural and symbolic associations with harmony, balance and 
the rhythm of nature, offering us a creative lens to tell a more expansive story about our origins and 
craft. As Rampur enters its second decade, this platform will anchor how the brand speaks to 
consumers across markets.” 
The natural positioning builds on Rampur’s growing international recognition. In Jim Murray’s Whisky 
Bible 2026, nine expressions from the Rampur portfolio featured with an average score of 91.9 points, 
a further marker of the brand’s standing among global whisky connoisseurs. Rampur has also 
strengthened its presence in international travel retail, becoming the first Indian single malt to be 
presented across four major UK airports at Heathrow, Gatwick, Manchester and Birmingham. 

 
Press Release 
 
 
The campaign is being rolled out across on-trade and retail touchpoints, including in-outlet branding, 
point-of-sale material and consumer experiences, to create a consistent expression of the platform 
wherever consumers encounter Rampur. It is complemented by digital storytelling featuring actor 
Mihir Ahuja, known for his role in Netflix’s Operation Safed Sagar, which brings the idea of 43° | 2° to a 
wider audience in a contemporary and accessible format. 
The announcement comes as Radico Khaitan continues to strengthen its premium and luxury 
portfolio. The Company’s Prestige & Above segment recorded 35.8% volume growth in Q1 FY2027, 
reaching 5.28 million cases and contributing 74% of its IMFL value sales. The Company has outlined 
an ambition to grow its luxury and semi-luxury portfolio by approximately 25% in FY2027. 
As Rampur enters its second decade, ‘43° | 2° - Born in Nature’s Frequency’ establishes a long-term 
platform for the brand across markets and consumer touchpoints. It returns the story to the forces 
that shape the whisky. The land, the changing seasons, the oak and the passage of time. 
Nature composed it. Oak held every note. 
 
[Please turn over for the brand creative] 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Saket Somani 
Deputy Chief Financial Officer  
somanis@radico.co.in | +91 11 4097 5403 
 
This release contains statements that contain “forward looking statements” including, but without limitation, 
statements relating to the implementation of strategic initiatives, and other statements relating to Radico

legislative developments, and other key factors that could affect our business and financial performance.

likely events or circumstances.

an ambition to grow its luxury and semi-luxury portfolio by approximately 25% in FY2027.

platform for the brand across markets and consumer touchpoints. It returns the story to the forces 
that shape the whisky. The land, the changing seasons, the oak and the passage of time. 
Nature composed it. Oak held every note.

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call 
of Uno Minda Limited. This conference call may contain forward-looking statements about the 
company, which are based on the beliefs, opinions, and expectations of the company as on the 
date of this call. These statements are not the guarantee of future performance of the company 
and may involve risks and uncertainties that are difficult to predict. 
As a reminder, all participants' line will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance 
during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touch-
tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Sunil Bohra, Group CFO. Thank you, and over to you, 
sir. 
Sunil Bohra: 
Thank you, Iqra. Good afternoon, everyone, and a warm welcome to all the participants. Happy 
Diwali and best wishes to you and your families. On the earnings call today, I am joined by my 
colleague, Ankur Modi. We have uploaded our financial results and investor presentation for the 
quarter and half year ending September 26 on the stock exchanges and our company's website. 
We hope everybody had an opportunity to go through the same. 
I will begin with a brief overview of the macroeconomic environment, followed by the current 
trends in the automotive industry, and then to our financial and operational performance for the 
quarter and half year ended September 26. Post that, we will open the floor for Q&A. 
Talking about the global economy, the global economic environment during the quarter 
remained challenging. The geopolitical conflicts have pushed up energy and commodity prices, 
disrupted key shipping and logistics routes, increased transportation and input costs for 
businesses across the world. As a result, the overall supply chain environment remains 
challenging. These factors are adding to inflationary pressures and weighing on global growth.  
According to the IMF's October 26 World Economic Outlook, global GDP is projected to slow 
to 3.1% for 2026, while global inflation projections have been revised upwards by 70 basis points 
to 4.7%. The outlook remains uncertain, and the duration of the conflict, along with its impact 
on energy supplies and global trade, will be the key factors to watch. 
Despite a challenging global backdrop, India continues to stand out as one of the brightest spots 
in the world economy. Our GDP grew 7.8% in Q1 FY27, ahead of expectations, and this 
momentum has been recognized globally. The IMF has raised India's FY27 growth forecast to 
7.0%, while RBI, in its October policy, revised its projection upward to 7.1% from 6.7% earlier. 
A stronger dollar has put pressure on the rupee, which, along with higher energy prices, has 
pushed up input costs. The RBI has responded proactively, raising its inflation projections to 
5.2% and increasing the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% to keep price stability firmly on 
track. 
Pllt•JI

Uno Minda Limited 
 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 11 
 
What gives us confidence is the strength of India's domestic market. Robust consumption, 
sustained government investment in infrastructure, and steady private capital spending continues 
to drive growth. At the same time, the government's focus on localization, manufacturing, digital 
transformation, and reforms are building an economy that can absorb external shocks far better 
than before. We believe this places India and business like ours in a strong position for long-
term growth. 
Moving to the automotive industry overview, for the second quarter of FY27, the Indian 
automotive industry sustained its strong momentum, with PV and two-wheeler segments 
recording their highest-ever quarterly production. The total automotive production crossed 109 
lakh units, a growth of around 18% year-on-year, while domestic sales rose 18.2% to 83.9 lakh 
units.

you, Mr. Jeewani.

Yes. Hi, good morning, everyone. This is Rahul from IIFL Capital. I welcome you all to the 
second quarter earnings conference call of KIMS Hospitals being hosted by IIFL. From KIMS, 
we have with us today Dr. Bhaskar Rao Bollineni, Founder and Managing Director, Dr. Abhinay 
Bollineni, Executive Director and CEO, Mr. Sachin Salvi, CFO, Dr. Nitish Kumar, the CEO for 
the Bangalore cluster, and Sreenath Reddy, Head of Business Development. Over to you, sir, for 
your opening comments. 
Bhaskar Rao Bollineni: 
Good morning, everyone. We are amidst a hectic festive season that commemorates the patriotic 
Independence Day, followed by DEVOTIONAL GANESH CHATURTHI, and recently 
concluded SPIRITUAL NAVRATRI. We are now on the threshold of JOYFUL DIWALI.  
                                               Let me start the meet by conveying our festive greetings to you. 
 
Now I am going to unfold the financial picture of Q2. I am sure the results I am going to 
announce now will wonderfully blend with the festive fervour. We have recorded a growth under 
all key parameters, both in quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year basis, with significant rise in 
revenue.  
                                                A snapshot of consolidated financial and operational highlights are as follows. 
 
Q2 FY 2027 updates:  
 Total revenue of INR1,363 crores, a growth of 41.3% on year-on-year and 14% on quarter-
on-quarter basis.  
 EBITDA of INR279 crores, a growth of 34% on year-on-year and 16.3% on quarter-on-
quarter basis. 
 EBITDA margin stood at 20.5% versus 20.1% in quarter one FY 2027, and 21.7% in quarter 
two FY 2026.  
 PAT at INR76 crores in quarter two, financial year 2027, against INR37 crores and INR72 
crores in quarter one FY 2027 and quarter two FY 2026, respectively.  
 Consolidated EPS for the period ended with 30th September 2026 of INR1.8, a growth of 
8.5% on year-on-year basis. 
 Cash and cash equivalents, including cash, bank balance, deposits with maturity of less than 
12 months, and investment in mutual funds of INR420 crores as on 30th September 2026.  
 
 

KIMS Hospital 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 18 
 
 
Q2 FY 2027 Financial Highlights – Consolidated: 
 Consolidated revenue from operations of INR1,344 crores, a growth of 39.9% on year-on-
year and 14% on quarter-on-quarter basis. 
 Consolidated EBITDA, pre-Ind AS, of INR250 crores. There is a growth of 24.7% on year-
on-year and 12.7% on quarter-on-quarter basis.  
 Consolidated EBITDA, pre-Ind AS, and excluding other income of INR232 crores, a growth

Operational Highlights Consolidated.

quarter basis, respectively. Average revenue per patient grew by 9.9% and 1.2% year-on-

I would like to apprise you about the acquisitions we have made recently to strengthen our

 KIMS Trust Hospital, Kakinada, 183 beds, we have acquired 51% of equity stake in Sarvottam

be known as the KIMS Trust Hospital. The acquisition holds high potential and prospectus. 
 
 Ushahkal Abhinav Specialty Hospital, Sangli, Maharashtra, with 316 beds. We have acquired 
6% stake by investing INR15 crores.  
 
 KIMS Kompally, Secunderabad, 225 beds.  
 
 KIMS Sikhara, Guntur, Andhra Pradesh, 150 beds.
