Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to KRBL Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference 
Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance 
during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touch-
tone phone. 
Please note that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Ashish 
Jain, Chief Financial Officer of KRBL Limited. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Ashish Jain: 
Thank you, and thank you for joining us. Welcome to the Q2 FY27 earnings conference call for 
analysts and investors of KRBL Limited. Today we have Mr. Anil Kumar Mittal, Chairman and 
Managing Director, Mr. Anoop Kumar Gupta, Joint Managing Director, Mr. Ayush Gupta, Head 
of the India Business, and Mr. Akshay Gupta, Head - Bulk Exports, as key speakers on the call.  
To begin the call, Mr. Anil Kumar Mittal will share updates on the business, industry, and our 
overall strategy. Following that, Mr. Ayush Gupta will provide insights into the performance 
and outlook of our domestic business. 
Finally, I will present the financial overview of the company for the second quarter and half year 
ended September 30, 2026. Once the management has concluded their opening remarks, we will 
open the floor for an interactive question-and-answer session. 
Please note that some of the statements made during the call may contain forward-looking 
information, and actual results may differ from these statements. You can refer to KRBL's 
investor presentation available on the stock exchange websites and our company’s website. 
Now, I would like to invite Anil ji to share his views. 
Anil Mittal: 
Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us for KRBL's Q2 FY27 earnings call. I will 
briefly cover the global and Indian rice outlook, the new basmati crop and paddy prices, the 
export environment, and the company's performance. Let me begin with global picture, which 
is broadly unchanged since our last call. As per USDA's October estimate, the world rice 
production in 2026-27 is expected to fall to 537 million tons from 546 million tons last year, 
with India accounting for most of the decline. 
 
Consumption, meanwhile, is expected to rise to a record of about 539 million tons. Global stocks 
are therefore expected to draw down. India continues to hold close to 30% of world rice trade, 
and USDA expects Indian exports of about 24 million tons in 2026-27, higher than the previous 
year. For India, USDA now estimates for 26-27 production at about 147 million metric tons 
against a record of 154 million tons last year, reflecting a weaker monsoon. 
India will remain alongside China, one of the two largest rice producers in the world, and 
domestic consumption is expected to rise by about 4 million tons. The 2026 monsoon ended 
about 13% below normal nationally, the weakest since 2015 under a strong El Nino. Last quarter, 
I flagged the risk this posed to the basmati belt. I am glad to say that risk largely did not 
materialize. Northwest India finished about 6% below normal. 

 
 
KRBL Limited 
 
 
November 03, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 17 
 
Irrigation carried the crop through, and trade estimates currently put the year's basmati crop 
modestly above last year's. The unseasonal rain in part of Punjab in the mid-October wet some 
harvested paddy in the mandis and flattened standing crop in places. The damage appears 
localized and will have a clear picture as arrivals progress. 
Despite a larger crop, basmati paddy prices have risen sharply. Major varieties are trading at 
around INR4,500-INR5,200 per quintal, well above last year's paddy price. There are three 
reasons. 
 
First, the industry has entered this season with almost no carryover stock. Second, the export 
realization have stayed high. And third, buyers across the Middle East need to rebuild depleted 
inventories, and the trade is pricing that demand in. Our procurement approach reflects this. We 
will not chase the market. 
 
We are buying in a staggered manner across the season with a firm focus on quality, low 
moisture, high recovery paddy. And our inventory position gives us the flexibility to be patient 
whenever prices run ahead of fundamentals. On exports, between April and August, India 
shipped about 2.5 million tons of basmati against 2.7 million tons in the same period last year. 
The entire decline was in the Middle East. Shipments to the rest of the world were unchanged. 
 
Realizations were about 21% higher in rupee terms. So, the rupee value of India's basmati export 
actually rose by around 12%. In August, volumes were back over last year's level. As I said last 
quarter, this remains a logistics problem and not a demand problem. 
 
The situation in the Gulf remains unsettled. Transit through the Strait of Hormuz has been 
intermittent, and freight and war risk premiums remain elevated and sensitive to every 
development. Marine cover continues to be available, priced shipment by shipment, and buyers 
have largely absorbed the higher cost because food security leaves them little alternative. 
Trade has adapted around the disruptions. Basmati shipment to Jordan, largely for onward 
movement to Iraq, are up almost six fold this year, more than offsetting the fall in direct 
shipments to Iraq. 
 
Iran is the exception. Payment and banking channels have become considerably more difficult 
since U.S. sanctions were tightened in August, and that market will take longer to normalize. 
Our view of recovery is unchanged. Inventories in the region are low, and when the route 
becomes dependable, restocking will be significant but we expect that normalization to be 
gradual rather than sudden. 
 
Now coming to KRBL's performance. KRBL recorded its highest-ever quarterly revenue of 
INR1,727 crores, up 14% on the same quarter last year, driven by 33% growth in domestic 
revenue. Export revenue for the first half was INR541 crores, lower by 41%. The decline was 
almost entirely in bulk export to the Middle East, where three factors weighted on the business. 
Payment channel in parts of the region became more difficult, movement through the Strait of 
Hormuz became more restricted, and weighing risk against reward. 

 
 
KRBL Limited 
 
 
November 03, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 17 
 
 
We chose to take on few opportunities there. We would rather protect the quality to our business 
than chase volume. At the same time, there are clear signs of strength. In second quarter, export 
revenue rose 22% over the first quarter to INR297 crores, although it remains 31% below last 
year. 
 
Exports to market outside the Middle East grew 14% in the first half. These markets are doing 
well and showing good growth, which reflects the diversification of our export business and a 
strong recall our brands enjoy. This is encouraging. Looking ahead, we expect exports to recover 
progressively through the second half, subject to condition in the Gulf. In Saudi Arabia, our

is broadly unchanged since our last call. As per USDA's October estimate, the world rice 
production in 2026-27 is expected to fall to 537 million tons from 546 million tons last year, 
with India accounting for most of the decline. 
 
Consumption, meanwhile, is expected to rise to a record of about 539 million tons. Global stocks 
are therefore expected to draw down. India continues to hold close to 30% of world rice trade, 
and USDA expects Indian exports of about 24 million tons in 2026-27, higher than the previous 
year. For India, USDA now estimates for 26-27 production at about 147 million metric tons 
against a record of 154 million tons last year, reflecting a weaker monsoon. 
India will remain alongside China, one of the two largest rice producers in the world, and 
domestic consumption is expected to rise by about 4 million tons. The 2026 monsoon ended 
about 13% below normal nationally, the weakest since 2015 under a strong El Nino. Last quarter, 
I flagged the risk this posed to the basmati belt. I am glad to say that risk largely did not 
materialize. Northwest India finished about 6% below normal. 

 
 
KRBL Limited 
 
 
November 03, 2026

Irrigation carried the crop through, and trade estimates currently put the year's basmati crop 
modestly above last year's. The unseasonal rain in part of Punjab in the mid-October wet some 
harvested paddy in the mandis and flattened standing crop in places. The damage appears 
localized and will have a clear picture as arrivals progress. 
Despite a larger crop, basmati paddy prices have risen sharply. Major varieties are trading at 
around INR4,500-INR5,200 per quintal, well above last year's paddy price. There are three 
reasons. 
 
First, the industry has entered this season with almost no carryover stock. Second, the export 
realization have stayed high. And third, buyers across the Middle East need to rebuild depleted 
inventories, and the trade is pricing that demand in. Our procurement approach reflects this. We 
will not chase the market. 
 
We are buying in a staggered manner across the season with a firm focus on quality, low 
moisture, high recovery paddy. And our inventory position gives us the flexibility to be patient 
whenever prices run ahead of fundamentals. On exports, between April and August, India 
shipped about 2.5 million tons of basmati against 2.7 million tons in the same period last year. 
The entire decline was in the Middle East. Shipments to the rest of the world were unchanged.

actually rose by around 12%. In August, volumes were back over last year's level. As I said last 
quarter, this remains a logistics problem and not a demand problem. 
 
The situation in the Gulf remains unsettled. Transit through the Strait of Hormuz has been 
intermittent, and freight and war risk premiums remain elevated and sensitive to every 
development. Marine cover continues to be available, priced shipment by shipment, and buyers 
have largely absorbed the higher cost because food security leaves them little alternative. 
Trade has adapted around the disruptions. Basmati shipment to Jordan, largely for onward 
movement to Iraq, are up almost six fold this year, more than offsetting the fall in direct 
shipments to Iraq. 
 
Iran is the exception. Payment and banking channels have become considerably more difficult 
since U.S. sanctions were tightened in August, and that market will take longer to normalize. 
Our view of recovery is unchanged. Inventories in the region are low, and when the route 
becomes dependable, restocking will be significant but we expect that normalization to be 
gradual rather than sudden.

INR1,727 crores, up 14% on the same quarter last year, driven by 33% growth in domestic

almost entirely in bulk export to the Middle East, where three factors weighted on the business.

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to EPL Limited Q2 FY27 Conference Call hosted 
by Systematix Shares & Stocks (India) Limited. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in 
the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the 
presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an 
operator by pressing star then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note that this conference is 
being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Raj Lakhani from Systematix. Thank you and over to 
you, sir. Please proceed. 
Raj Lakhani: 
Thank you. Good evening, everyone. On behalf of Systematix Institutional Equities, I welcome 
you all to the Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Call of EPL Limited. The management team is 
represented by Mr. Hemant Bakshi, MD and Global CEO; Mr. M.R. Ramasamy, COO;  
Mr. Deepak Goyal, CFO; and Mr. Onkar Ghangurde, Head, Legal, Company Secretary and 
Compliance Officer. We would like to thank the management for giving us the opportunity to 
host this call. 
 
I will now hand over the call to the management for their opening remarks, post which we will 
have the Q&A session. Thank you. And over to you, sir. 
Hemant Bakshi: 
Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us for EPL Limited's Quarter 2 FY27 
Earnings Call. I'm happy to report that EPL has delivered another standout quarter, achieving 
robust growth while maintaining margins, demonstrating the resilience of our business and our 
ability to navigate a volatile operating environment. Revenue for the quarter grew by 30%. This 
is the highest ever growth that EPL has ever declared. EBITDA increased by 17.6%, with 
reported EBITDA margins at 18.9%. 
 
On an underlying basis, excluding the pass-through impact of higher raw material prices, 
revenue grew by 20.3%, with underlying EBITDA margins at 20.4%. Our growth was broad-
based across categories and geographies. Beauty & Cosmetics delivered exceptional 
performance at 42.9% growth, while Oral Care continued its strong performance with a growth 
of 19.2%. 
 
In the month of September, B&C revenues exceeded that of Oral Care, becoming our largest 
category. This is a significant milestone and clear demonstration that our strategy is delivering 
in full and investments being made in this segment are translating into growth and market share 
gains. 
 
Regionally, we delivered strong performance across all markets. EAP led with revenue growth 
of 40%, followed by Europe at 30%, AMESA at 28% and Americas at 25%. India stand-alone 
also delivered robust growth of 30%. The breadth of this performance across regions reflects our 
ability to capture growth opportunities across diverse markets. 
 
Our EBITDA continued its strong momentum, growing by 17.6% and marking our 16th 
consecutive quarter of double-digit EBITDA growth, demonstrating our ability to sustain growth 
while maintaining profitability. 

 
 
EPL Limited 
 
 
November 4, 2026 
Page 3 of 16 
 
 
Despite continued cost pressures, we have successfully recovered the full impact of cost 
increases through pricing actions. This has enabled us to maintain underlying EBITDA margins 
above 20%, while continuing to fund our growth priorities. We have invested ahead of the curve. 
Capex investments in H1 2027 was INR3,150 million, which is almost 90% increase over the 
same period of last year. This has translated into record revenue growth. 
 
We are very confident that our business has momentum, and these investments will continue to 
translate into growth and build a sustainable competitive advantage for our business. PAT during 
this quarter grew by 5.6% due to higher depreciation, higher effective tax rate as a result of 
country mix and adverse forex movements. While we will sustain investments for future growth, 
this will be alongside a strong focus on capital efficiency. 
 
Geopolitical environment: We operate in a challenging global environment. The ongoing 
conflict in Middle East is keeping commodity prices elevated and disrupting supply chains. Our 
objectives during this crisis have been - one, ensure superior uninterrupted service to our 
customers globally; and two, full recovery of the cost through price. 
 
We have fully met both these objectives. Going the extra mile to deliver superior service, 
including bearing higher cost of air freight, if necessary, we are being rewarded through gain in 
market share as a result of these bold actions. At the same time, we have fully recovered elevated 
costs through pricing. 
 
Sustainability, innovation and people practices: Innovation continues to be a key differentiator 
for EPL. Through close collaboration and co-creation with our customers, we are developing 
tailored solutions across product categories that help brands stand out on the shelf, meet evolving 
consumer needs and deliver greater value. 
 
We have also advanced our sustainable packaging portfolio, with sustainable tubes accounting 
for 41% of our product mix. Our achievements have been recognized through multiple awards 
at the IFCA Star Awards for Innovation and at the Print Week Awards across various categories. 
 
Behind this progress are our people whose commitment and contribution are pivotal to the 
success of EPL. We are proud that our operations in seven countries are certified as Great Place 
to Work, reflecting our commitment to building a positive, engaging and thriving workplace. 
 
Looking ahead, let me start with an update on our proposed merger with Indovida. We are 
encouraged by the progress so far, having received approvals from the Competition Commission 
of India, foreign antitrust authorities and the stock exchanges. We have now filed our application 
with the National Company Law Tribunal, bringing us a step closer to the important milestone 
for EPL, with the process advancing as planned. 
 
We remain confident of completing the merger within the expected timeline and look forward 
to realizing the opportunities this combination presents. Our priorities for the future are clear 
and unchanged. 
 
 
 
 

 
 
EPL Limited 
 
 
November 4, 2026 
Page 4 of 16 
 
First, strengthen our leadership in Beauty & Cosmetics. The momentum over the last few 
quarters has been encouraging, but we believe the opportunity ahead remains significant. There 
is considerable scope to expand across additional categories, customers and markets, providing 
a strong runway for continued growth. Our proactive investments in capex, innovation, extrusion 
capabilities and front-end specialization position us well to capture this opportunity and sustain 
our growth momentum. 
 
Second, accelerating growth in high-potential markets. Emerging markets continue to offer 
attractive opportunities, supported by evolving consumer preferences and increasing demand for 
differentiated packaging. 
 
Thailand is progressing well, backed by a strong customer pipeline, while Brazil is a strong 
example of our ability to build momentum and translate market opportunities into sustained 
growth. At the same time, we are exploring other markets for entry in the near future.  
Third, sustaining margins with improving capital efficiency. As we invest for growth, we remain 
focused on productivity, cost discipline and operational excellence across our global operations. 
Our priority is to sustain underlying EBITDA margins at 20% plus while ensuring disciplined 
capital allocation and attractive return on our investments. 
 
Fourth, expanding beyond tubes into broader consumer packaging. Our long-term ambition is to 
build a leading consumer packaging business for the emerging markets, extending beyond our 
existing product formats. The proposed merger with Indovida is an important step, providing an 
opportunity to broaden our portfolio across new markets and customer segments and unlock 
synergies over time while building on our leadership in tubes. 
 
Beyond this, we continue to evaluate opportunities to expand further into consumer packaging, 
with a focus on strategic fit and long-term value creation. We remain confident in our ability to 
navigate the evolving external environment while continuing to execute our strategic priorities. 
 
Our performance this quarter reflects the strength of our business and the progress we continue 
to make. We are retaining our near-term guidance of revenue growth in high teens and 
underlying margins of 20%. As we look ahead, we remain focused on building on this 
momentum and creating sustainable long-term value for all our stakeholders. 
 
Thank you for your continued support and trust. We will now open the floor for questions.

declined. Can you throw some light what's actually happening in Europe? That has been a little 
zigzag. We do well for a couple of quarters, then we slip away. Are we taking measures to see

Hemant Bakshi: 
Yes. So as I mentioned that our capex in the first half of the year has been INR315 crores.

has been 30.4%. In a mature market, which doesn't show much growth as a market overall to 
grow 30% in the midst of a crisis, we think is a very good performance. So, we are very happy 
with growth. 
 
Having said that, there have been operational challenges over a period of time in Europe. These 
have been deeper and more stubborn to resolve than what we had originally anticipated. I want 
to take you through a bit of detail on what has happened in Europe and what we are doing.

the fact that our cost centers in Eastern Europe are at a lower level compared to Western Europe. 
So, we had decided to centralize some of our operations in Poland, one of which was printing. 
 
And in our printing site, which we had found in Poland, it took us much longer to get regulatory 
approvals than what we had anticipated. It took us at least 6 to 9 months longer. And while we've 
continued to have higher demand, as this stabilization has taken some time, it has led to higher 
outsourcing costs. 
 
Having said that, we have now fully got all approvals and we are in the process of managing the 
transition from one plant to the other. Overall, we feel that it will take us another 2 to 3 quarters 
to fully stabilize operations and get margins back to the levels at which we want them to be. 
While there have been challenges in the recent past, we remain very confident and very positive 
about our business in Europe.

Management Commentary (1/2)
I am happy to inform that Texmaco Rail has delivered an improved performance for Q2 of FY 26-27 in comparison to Q1 26-27
Our financial trajectory this quarter reflects operational efficiency and market diversification :
Top-Line Growth: Revenue from operations reached Rs 863 Crore, marking a strong 14.6% sequential growth from Rs 753 Crore in Q1.
Profitability: Profit Before Tax (PBT) rose to Rs 51.2 Crore, up from Rs 44.1 Crore in the previous sequential quarter.
Segment wise breakdown of revenue expansion in Q2 over Q1 26-27 is as follows:
Freight Car: Up 3.8%.
Railway Infrastructure: Up 41.7%.
Infrastructure Electrical: Up 38%.
In response to a reduction in Freight Car orders from Indian Railways, we have actively diversified our order book to capture higher-margin, 
resilient revenue streams:
Private & Export Markets: We expanded our outreach to private domestic customers and unlocked strategic export channels, targeting freight 
car demand in Africa and high-value rail components in the US. This shift has not only driven our current quarter’s growth but establishes a 
more diversified order book compared to this time last year.
To secure long-term value, we are aggressively expanding our technical capabilities and footprint across three massive growth pillars:
Global Leasing Scale: Texmaco has strengthened its railcar leasing business, with the induction of Trinity Rail as a joint venture partner into its 
JV - Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing. This partnership brings together global fleet management expertise and an established leasing platform 
which will build the foundation for the company to expand its railcar leasing business.
Digital Rail Infra & Safety: We are exploring collaboration with Global partners for digitalisation and advanced train control systems, including 
the development of Kavach solutions for the Indian market. This moves Texmaco up the value chain, allowing us to command a much wider 
scope of work in large-scale infrastructure projects.
Defence Capabilities Unlock: Texmaco also made progress in developing its defence business with Vagus Def Tech  & Aerospace Fund 
acquiring a 30% equity stake in Texmaco Defence Technologies Ltd (TDTL). This will help TDTL to develop capabilities as  a preferred supplier for 
multiple defence projects in India.  
The performance this quarter reinforces our core mission: strengthening Texmaco’s competitive positioning while unlocking sustainable new 
areas for growth.
Standalone Financials

5
Management Commentary (2/2)
Sudipta Mukherjee
Managing Director
I am pleased to share an update on the Company's performance for the second quarter of FY27.
Standalone Revenue from Operations stood at ₹863 crore, registering sequential growth of 14.6%. EBITDA margin remained 
resilient at 10.2%, notwithstanding elevated input costs. Importantly, after adjusting for non-recurring items in Q1 FY27, the 
current quarter recorded an improvement of 0.70 bps in EBITDA from core operating activities, reflecting an underlying 
improvement in operational performance.
Despite a significant reduction in the Indian Railways order book compared with SPLY (Q2 FY26), our diversification strategy 
has begun delivering tangible results. The Freight Car business has witnessed a turnaround, with sequential revenue growth 
of 3.75% and an EBITDA margin growth 60 bps. This improvement is a result of focused cost rationalisation and a better 
product mix, which has helped mitigate inflationary pressures.
Our Infra-Electrical business continued its growth momentum, recording a sequential revenue increase of 37.6%. Infra-Rail & 
Green Energy also delivered improved revenues and profitability, supported by disciplined project execution.
Our consolidated order book increased by 10.2% during the quarter to ₹10,940 crore as at September 30, 2026. More 
recently, we secured an additional Freight Car order worth ₹412 crore from Indian Railways. The continued traction from 
private-sector customers, alongside orders from Indian Railways, reinforces the growing breadth of our customer franchise.
On the institutional front, the Company received an upgraded CRISIL A+/Stable rating for its long-term bank facilities. Our 
ESG score also improved from 51 to 59, reflecting progress in our sustainability and governance initiatives.
Looking ahead, we see significant opportunities across Freight cars, components, wheels and associated infrastructure. Our 
Infra-Electrical and Rail Projects businesses continue to strengthen their growth trajectories. 
Our strategic forays into Passenger Mobility and Defence have also made meaningful progress during the quarter, promising 
avenues for future growth.
As we move forward, our focus remains on building a more diversified, resilient and competitive enterprise, with sustainable 
profitability, execution excellence and an expanding presence in higher-value businesses.
We thank our shareholders, customers, employees and all stakeholders for their continued trust and confidence.

Texmaco: Brief Note (1/2)
1. Sustained Leadership in Freight Cars
• One of the largest suppliers of Freight Cars in India, manufacturing one out of every four Wagons on the IR network
• Manufacturing record of 50,000+ Freight Cars supplied over the last 20 years, including 7,000+ Freight Cars supplied to private customers over the last 10 years
• Portfolio of 20+ Freight Car variants catering to diverse end-industry applications, supported by manufacturing capacity of 2,500–3,000 wagons per quarter
2. Leading Exporter of Railway Castings from India
• Leading position in the export of Freight Cars and railway components for 50 years
• Export track record of 550+ Freight Cars to international markets over 3 years
• One of the leading exporter of railway castings from India, supplying to global markets and benefiting from geopolitical shifts in supply chains
3. Cost Optimised Manufacturing Platform
• Freight Car and components: 4 sites at Agarpara, Belgharia, Panihati and Sodepur in West Bengal and 1 in Vadodara, Gujarat
• 2 Foundry facilities: 33,000 MTPA Belgharia, West Bengal and 15,000 MTPA Raipur, Chhattisgarh
• One of the largest foundry to be accredited by the Association of American Railroad (AAR)
• A leading company working with mild-steel, stainless steel and composite materials for manufacturing of rolling stock solutions
4. Strategic and Technology Based Partnerships
• Touax Texmaco (34%): leases Freight Cars on long term basis to private sector logistics and industrial transportation companies in India
• Nymwag Texmaco (51%): to manufacture Freight Wagons and railway components for IR, the private sector and export markets
• Wabtec Texmaco (40%): manufactures world class braking systems and components for the Indian and US markets
• Saira Asia (51%): manufactures passenger coach railway interiors in Vadodara

14
Texmaco: Brief Note (2/2)
5. Core Business Focus and Core Business Expectation
• Optimise new designs and introduce them in India
• Increase focus on Systems & Solutions, Signalling and Safety Solutions within the Infra – Rail & Green Energy business
• Building new growth platforms through Renewable Energy and Defence businesses
• Embedding technology across operations through AI, Digital Engineering, Automation and Predictive O&M
6. Attractive Railway Industry Dynamics
• 8 new railway reforms announced by the Government
• Indian Railways plan for Rs. 13 Lakhs crore Freight Led-Expansion
• Initiatives such as Vande Bharat, Kavach, Dedicated Freight Corridors and Station Redevelopment continue to expand opportunities across the rail value chain
• Make in India, localisation initiatives and global supply chain diversification continue to support manufacturing, components and export opportunities
• India's first Vande Bharat Freight EMU successfully achieved 145 kmph during trials, supporting the development of high-speed freight logistics for time-sensitive 
cargo, e-commerce, parcels and cold-chain transportation

Management Commentary (1/2)
I am happy to inform that Texmaco Rail has delivered an improved performance for Q2 of FY 26-27 in comparison to Q1 26-27
Our financial trajectory this quarter reflects operational efficiency and market diversification :
Top-Line Growth: Revenue from operations reached Rs 863 Crore, marking a strong 14.6% sequential growth from Rs 753 Crore in Q1.
Profitability: Profit Before Tax (PBT) rose to Rs 51.2 Crore, up from Rs 44.1 Crore in the previous sequential quarter.
Segment wise breakdown of revenue expansion in Q2 over Q1 26-27 is as follows:
Freight Car: Up 3.8%.
Railway Infrastructure: Up 41.7%.
Infrastructure Electrical: Up 38%.
In response to a reduction in Freight Car orders from Indian Railways, we have actively diversified our order book to capture higher-margin, 
resilient revenue streams:
Private & Export Markets: We expanded our outreach to private domestic customers and unlocked strategic export channels, targeting freight 
car demand in Africa and high-value rail components in the US. This shift has not only driven our current quarter’s growth but establishes a 
more diversified order book compared to this time last year.
To secure long-term value, we are aggressively expanding our technical capabilities and footprint across three massive growth pillars:
Global Leasing Scale: Texmaco has strengthened its railcar leasing business, with the induction of Trinity Rail as a joint venture partner into its 
JV - Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing. This partnership brings together global fleet management expertise and an established leasing platform 
which will build the foundation for the company to expand its railcar leasing business.
Digital Rail Infra & Safety: We are exploring collaboration with Global partners for digitalisation and advanced train control systems, including 
the development of Kavach solutions for the Indian market. This moves Texmaco up the value chain, allowing us to command a much wider 
scope of work in large-scale infrastructure projects.
Defence Capabilities Unlock: Texmaco also made progress in developing its defence business with Vagus Def Tech  & Aerospace Fund 
acquiring a 30% equity stake in Texmaco Defence Technologies Ltd (TDTL). This will help TDTL to develop capabilities as  a preferred supplier for 
multiple defence projects in India.  
The performance this quarter reinforces our core mission: strengthening Texmaco’s competitive positioning while unlocking sustainable new 
areas for growth.

Management Commentary (2/2)
Sudipta Mukherjee
Managing Director
I am pleased to share an update on the Company's performance for the second quarter of FY27.
Standalone Revenue from Operations stood at ₹863 crore, registering sequential growth of 14.6%. EBITDA margin remained 
resilient at 10.2%, notwithstanding elevated input costs. Importantly, after adjusting for non-recurring items in Q1 FY27, the 
current quarter recorded an improvement of 0.70 bps in EBITDA from core operating activities, reflecting an underlying 
improvement in operational performance.
Despite a significant reduction in the Indian Railways order book compared with SPLY (Q2 FY26), our diversification strategy 
has begun delivering tangible results. The Freight Car business has witnessed a turnaround, with sequential revenue growth 
of 3.75% and an EBITDA margin growth 60 bps. This improvement is a result of focused cost rationalisation and a better 
product mix, which has helped mitigate inflationary pressures.
Our Infra-Electrical business continued its growth momentum, recording a sequential revenue increase of 37.6%. Infra-Rail & 
Green Energy also delivered improved revenues and profitability, supported by disciplined project execution.
Our consolidated order book increased by 10.2% during the quarter to ₹10,940 crore as at September 30, 2026. More 
recently, we secured an additional Freight Car order worth ₹412 crore from Indian Railways. The continued traction from 
private-sector customers, alongside orders from Indian Railways, reinforces the growing breadth of our customer franchise.
On the institutional front, the Company received an upgraded CRISIL A+/Stable rating for its long-term bank facilities. Our 
ESG score also improved from 51 to 59, reflecting progress in our sustainability and governance initiatives.
Looking ahead, we see significant opportunities across Freight cars, components, wheels and associated infrastructure. Our 
Infra-Electrical and Rail Projects businesses continue to strengthen their growth trajectories. 
Our strategic forays into Passenger Mobility and Defence have also made meaningful progress during the quarter, promising 
avenues for future growth.
As we move forward, our focus remains on building a more diversified, resilient and competitive enterprise, with sustainable 
profitability, execution excellence and an expanding presence in higher-value businesses.
We thank our shareholders, customers, employees and all stakeholders for their continued trust and confidence.

Randeep Narang:

Deepak, as already mentioned. So I'm very pleased to share that Transrail has delivered very 
strong Q2 '27 performance, recording the highest ever revenue and EBITDA. 
 
This robust performance is achieved despite the continued impact on supply chain and logistics 
due to the Middle East/west asia crisis. This reflects better execution momentum across our 
projects, sharp focus on cash flow management. With this, the company's overall H1 
performance is back on track to achieve the annual growth guidance. 
 
Since listing, we have not missed any of our revenue or margin guidance, and we continue to be 
confident to achieve the same trend this year. Our focus remains on sustaining this growth while 
striving for industry-leading profitability and cash generation. Speaking of the numbers, the 
revenue for operations for quarter end September 30, has grown to INR2,056 crores, which is a 
32% jump year-on-year. Similarly, EBITDA stood at INR238 crores, which is a 28% jump year-
on-year, quarter 2. 
 
Alongside our operating performance, we've continued to strengthen our balance sheet. Our cash 
flow from operations was impressive INR435 crores in H1, while the net working capital cycle 
days is sustained at 82 days for the same period. It reflects our continued focus on collections, 
project execution milestones, efficient working capital management. Going forward, improving 
cash conversion will remain an important priority as we scale up our operations further.

tower manufacturing capacity currently stands at 1,84,400 metric tons per annum, while

40,800 kilometers per annum. We have progressed well with our planned capex investments to 
further strengthen our manufacturing base.

supply assurance and have greater control of quality and delivery to meet the customer 
expectations. Our order book stands at INR14,218 crores as of September 30. While post the 
quarter got over, we have already declared orders of INR1,747 crores, providing strong revenue 
visibility. 
 
With this improvement in order momentum, we are confident to achieve an annual order intake 
of INR10,000-plus crores, while maintaining a healthy book-to-bill ratio. The order win is also 
encouraging from the business diversification perspective, spanning transmission, substation, 
conductor and re-conducting opportunity. An important development is the order wins we've 
had and we have awarded -- got awarded 5 conductor jobs in India, where we will use our own 
manufactured carbon core HTLS conductors. 
 
We see this as an important product breakthrough for Transrail. reconductoring provides an 
opportunity to enhance the existing transmission corridors without requiring the development of 
entirely new transmission routes. Our entry into these projects with our own manufactured HTLS 
conductor strengthens our presence in the conductor segment and opens up additional 
opportunity in transmission infrastructure market. 
 
Further, we've also started booking small quantities for U.S. and other developed markets. We 
also recently secured greenfield GIS project in Jordan, which is 400kV and 765 kV transmission 
lines in India.  
                                                Looking ahead, we believe the structural opportunity in India power transmission and 
distribution sector remains strong. Rising electricity demand, renewable energy capacity 
additions, increasing electrification and need to strengthen and modernize the national grid has 
created a sustained requirement for transmission lines, substations, HVDC infrastructure and 
associated power infrastructure. 
 
We believe that not merely a near-term opportunity, but multi-decadal growth drivers are 
available in the power infrastructure industry. The scale of investments envisaged across the 
sector provides encouraging visibility for experienced EPC players like Transrail with 
meaningful opportunity in the next 5 years up to 2032. 
 
With the broader growth opportunity programs, Green Energy Corridor, Phase 3, GEC-III, we 
expect to play an important role. The program envisages an outlay of approximately 
INR1,86,000 crores, including INR1.36 lakh crores only for intra-state transmission and 
INR50,000 crores for battery storage. Most of this is expected in TBCB model, and hence, we 
expect our existing large client to be well positioned for such projects and hence, the addressable 
market for us will improve over the years. 
 
As part of strategic diversification and leverage our core T&D expertise, we are evaluating 
opportunities and complementing our existing capabilities. In this context, the Board has

12%. The factors relating to it is like depreciation has increased by 35% and interest cost has 
also increased. And taxes have increased a lot.

doing, it has increased. But on the interest and the taxes because the tax rate has also gone up. 
So any color on reference to that, please?

So I'll request Mr. Rajesh, our Group CFO, to address this question. Principally, you already 
answered half of the answer. We can only add a little bit more. 
Rajesh Neelkanthan: 
So on the interest component, since the all working capital funded limits, interest cost has 
marginally gone up on an absolute basis compared to our revenue because as we continue to 
grow, our interest cost also marginally grow. But as a percentage, we see it coming down to 
revenue. 
 
On the taxes, it's a one-off case which we have provided in September, and that's about it. For 
the future, we see the tax rate coming back to what it normally is around 25%, 26%. This was a 
one-off scenario for this quarter. And going forward, it will be normalized. 
Yash Kabra:

November 04, 2026

is one of the kind of thing in investor presentation, you are benchmarking yourself and also 
showing that how you performed against the guidance, that's a good sign. 
 
First question is regarding HTLS conductor, sir. So we are getting the reconductoring orders. So

parts of the country, as in this case, West Bengal and Tamil Nadu. And this will carry 30% more 
electricity through the HTLS conductor. So therefore, it is grid strengthening without investing 
heavily into capex for new line. 
 
Whereas we have a lot of new opportunities through solar power generated transmission line 
requirements. And both will run independently. Of course, new line potential is much higher. 
We're talking about going up to INR9 lakh-odd crores by '30, '32. This is smaller, and this is

solution provider. So solar power generation was what we found the most natural fit where using

November 04, 2026 
 
Page 8 of 15
